root_cause.text: `bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail()` in `net/core/filter.c` computed XDP fragment tailroom from `rxq->frag_size` using an `unsigned int`, so when drivers supplied a DMA write size instead of a true fragment size the subtraction could underflow on a non-zero page offset and turn a negative tailroom into a huge positive value, bypassing the intended `-EINVAL` check.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `tailroom` from `unsigned int` to `int` and adds `WARN_ON_ONCE(tailroom < 0)`, while the CVE text explicitly says `rxq->frag_size` “expects a truesize,” negative tailroom occurs “because there is a non-zero page offset,” and “due to tailroom being stored as an unsigned int, it is reported to be somewhere near UINT_MAX, resulting in a tail being grown.”

Author: Eelco Chaudron <echaudro@redhat.com>
Date:   Fri Jan 21 11:09:55 2022 +0100

    bpf: add frags support to the bpf_xdp_adjust_tail() API
    
    This change adds support for tail growing and shrinking for XDP frags.
    
    When called on a non-linear packet with a grow request, it will work
    on the last fragment of the packet. So the maximum grow size is the
    last fragments tailroom, i.e. no new buffer will be allocated.

In this commit, `bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail()` computes `tailroom` as `unsigned int tailroom;` followed by `tailroom = rxq->frag_size - skb_frag_size(frag) - skb_frag_off(frag);` and only checks `if (unlikely(offset > tailroom)) return -EINVAL;`. However, the commit also explicitly requires `rxq->frag_size` to be valid via `if (!rxq->frag_size || rxq->frag_size > xdp->frame_sz) return -EOPNOTSUPP;`, which prevents the zero-size case and constrains the configured fragment size. The specific bug root cause—drivers supplying DMA write size instead of true fragment size causing underflow on a non-zero page offset and bypassing the `-EINVAL` check—is not shown as a flaw in this code body alone, and the code already contains the added frags support logic rather than an obvious missing guard. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent in the shown snippet, and this function body does not let us mark the bug as present.
